Alpha 1.0.45 (room to recover)

  • Slower passive recovery: Health and mana regeneration now grant 0.01 points per second for each point of Vitality or Wisdom. The old tooltips advertised 0.1, but the actual formulas used 0.5; both the server and offline game now use the requested 0.01 rate.
  • Small amounts still count: The server retains fractional regeneration between ticks, so 10 Vitality or Wisdom restores one point over ten seconds instead of rounding every tick down to zero. Full or dead characters cannot bank unused recovery. Active healing and separately described equipment effects are unchanged.
  • Starting-ability runes: Level-unlocked runes for Charge, Piercing Throw, Fireball and Spirit Guardians now equip without first choosing a specialization. Other skills and rune level requirements remain locked until earned.
  • Read an effect, keep your view: Phone status details now fit short lists instead of stretching a mostly empty window over your character. Empty panels stay small, and a single shield leaves the center of portrait play visible.
  • More effects, not smaller text: Long buff and debuff lists remain independently scrollable within a bounded panel. Full names and descriptions keep their readable size; effect type and remaining time share a compact row.
  • Controls stay within reach: Portrait and short landscape retain their thumb-control space, a full-size Close button and permanent chat access. Shield values and timers still follow the server.
  • Independent overnight checks: Multiplayer soak checks now use isolated ports, binaries and evidence, and verify their own server before sending load. Other projects' services are left alone; the 100-client and resource-usage checks remain required.
  • Still being refined: This improves the status panel, not the entire phone interface. Entrance scenery can still obscure combat, and physical-phone ergonomics and performance testing remain open.

Alpha 1.0.44 (a ward worth training)

  • A stronger ward: Arcane Shield Mastery now adds 4% damage absorption per rank, up to 20%. Each cast keeps its trained capacity until the shield breaks or expires.
  • Focus stays yours: Shield absorption is separate from spell damage. Casting a shield neither spends Spell Focus nor uses its damage bonus to inflate protection.
  • Training that stays with you: Mastery survives a fresh login, the Effects panel shows the remaining shield, and normal hostile attacks consume the protection. Existing duration training and Extended continue to compose.
  • A dependable fallback ward: Offline shields use the same capacity, duration, mana cost and cooldown. Locked casts do not spend mana, and broken or expired shields clear their remaining protection and effect.
  • Still being refined: Offline Reflective and Explosive rune parity, entrance visibility, compact phone status details and the broader class and physical-phone reviews remain open.

Alpha 1.0.43 (an ally that answers)

  • A summon that answers: Avenging Seraph summons at your side without chasing the cursor. It and Spirit Guardians can be cast from the hotbar without aiming at the ground.
  • Training your celestial ally: Seraph Mastery increases its smite damage and Technique extends its lifetime. Each summon remembers its training and duration when cast, including the existing set extension.
  • An ally that respects the dungeon: Seraph attacks and following respect dungeon walls. Summons leave when their owner dies, disconnects or changes instances; damage and defeat credit remain with the owner.
  • A clearer smite: Repeated Seraph action labels use compact, above-character text on desktop as well as phone, retaining attribution without a wide line across the fight.
  • A real fallback companion: The offline fallback now creates a visible, attacking, following ally with normal expiry and cleanup. Normal login remains multiplayer; this is not a separate offline campaign mode.
  • Still being refined: Full class and rune balance, remaining offline differences, encounter visibility and physical-phone playability continue toward the larger roadmap milestones.

Alpha 1.0.42 (every wound remembers)

  • Mastery in every wound: Shadow Lunge, Serrated Edges and Poison Coating now apply their trained damage to bleed and poison ticks. Five Mastery ranks grant the advertised 20% bonus, with saved ranks preserved.
  • One hit, one calculation: Serrated Edges inherits its initiating projectile's damage without multiplying equipment, generic training or critical bonuses a second time. Its Mastery does not boost the separate Serrated rune while the buff is inactive.
  • Offline wounds stay honest: Bleed and poison retain their attacker and application-time damage, keep ticking through stuns, and clear cleanly on cleanse, expiry or death. Coated basic attacks now apply poison offline; online damage remains server-owned.
  • Enemies remain within reach: Overlapping dungeon entrance geometry no longer steals enemy selection. Entrances remain available for normal interaction when no higher-priority target covers the pointer.
  • Clearer training: Close-Quarters Grace now describes its existing 2% skill-damage bonus per rank instead of incorrectly promising 3% melee damage.
  • Still being refined: Broader talent balance, remaining offline ability differences, mobile ergonomics and the larger roadmap milestones remain in progress.

Alpha 1.0.41 (training with a critical edge)

  • Critical training counts: Applicable critical-chance talents now contribute alongside equipment on attacks, damaging abilities and their retained effects. Rogue Technique applies to its own skill; its text, Needle Precision and Edge Awareness now describe their actual critical bonuses.
  • One decisive critical: Backstab's Cloak combo and Ambush rune share one ordinary critical with equipment and training, after armor. They no longer multiply the same critical repeatedly; Lucky remains a separate proc.
  • Fire that respects the fight: Fireball splash starts at 40% of raw damage and evaluates each target's modifiers separately. Implosion checks whether each recipient is slowed, and solid dungeon walls block splash.
  • Offline hits with feedback: Implemented offline attacks, damaging skills and periodic effects consume critical training and preserve the attacking character. Critical hits receive explicit feedback; local projectile flight and splash respect dungeon walls without predicting online damage.
  • Builds that stay trained: Real-server checks cover normal critical-talent purchases, targeted primary attacks and saved ranks after a fresh login for Rogue, Wizard and Fighter.
  • Still being refined: The broader talent audit, remaining offline abilities and rune differences, class balance and full dungeon/raid validation remain in progress.

Alpha 1.0.40 (clearer rites, clearer battles)

  • Training reaches the edge: Battlefield Ministry now expands Radiant Strike, Healing Light's Beacon and the Mass Revival combo. Their visible boundaries match the accepted cast for you and nearby players.
  • Help where it belongs: Beacon follows the actual healing target, Mass Revival centers on the caster, and ordinary Healing Light stays single-target. A corrected cast updates its boundary without replaying your animation.
  • Strike the enemy you can reach: Radiant Strike's touch, click and chase range checks account for trained reach and large enemy bodies on the ground plane.
  • More dependable offline rites: Healing Light uses its proper healing, cooldown, Beacon and normal Mass Revival sequence; Renewal ticks on its recipient and Divine cleanses one debuff. Radiant Strike respects its cone, dungeon walls, mastery and runes. Online health remains server-owned.
  • Readable action, clear encounter: Phone actor-action labels stay bounded above their characters, retain readable action text and shorten long names visually. Combos keep their compact notification without a second oversized label across the hero; desktop feedback is unchanged.
  • Short lunges count: Shadow Lunge now confirms its actual landing to your client, including short steps behind nearby enemies. Small movements no longer disappear into position smoothing; target choice, dungeon-wall restrictions and bleed remain authoritative.
  • Still being refined: Broader class balance, remaining offline ability differences and physical-phone playtesting continue toward the larger roadmap milestones.

Alpha 1.0.39 (your party within reach)

  • A view around your controls: Phone camera framing now follows the space reserved for encounters, including horizontal framing in landscape. Default character scale and your manual zoom remain unchanged when opening menus or chat.
  • Room for both thumbs: Short landscape arranges your four skills in a two-by-two group, moves Effects to the left and keeps the full map available through Menu.
  • Your party, when you need it: A Party button opens readable, scrolling member details and party actions. Health updates preserve your reading position instead of rebuilding the panel over the world.
  • Choose who receives your help: Select an ally in Party before casting Healing Light or Divine Intervention. Attacks retain their separate enemy target; unavailable selected allies and out-of-range casts give feedback.
  • Feedback without blocked controls: Expanded chat stays above the quest tracker so its close control remains usable. Phone combo notices are compact and never intercept touches.
  • Still being refined: These improvements do not complete the broader phone redesign or real-device, dungeon and group-play verification.

Alpha 1.0.38 (room for the adventure)

  • Small guardians, dependable reach: Spirit Guardians and Boost use their trained area, including Expanded, for real periodic effects. Their exact perimeter follows the caster without enlarging the cherubs; late-joining players receive the active radius, rune and remaining time.
  • One row for your journey: Tap the compact phone objective to open the Journal, or use its next arrow to cycle all your tracked quests. Larger text and a single row leave more of the world visible without changing your tracking choices.
  • Notices that make room: Level-up and combat notices now expire, restoring your selected target when appropriate. Phone self-buff feedback no longer repeats your full character name across the world.
  • Better short-screen fit: Landscape health bars and objectives no longer overlap, and the Journal keeps chat uncovered on short phones. Town and dungeon guidance remains visible in the compact tracker.
  • Chat stays within reach: Expanded phone chat sits above the compact quest tracker, so its controls remain tappable after rotating into landscape. Collapse chat to return to your tracked objective.
  • Short blinks count: Teleport now applies its accepted landing even over very short distances, clearing the old movement path so a wall-clipped blink is not lost to position smoothing.
  • Safer shared combat: Damage and lifesteal reporting no longer races newly spawned loot during simultaneous Whirlwind attacks.
  • The right milestones: Level-up guidance names the actual level 30, 60 and 70 dungeon unlocks. Reaching level 100 correctly announces Heroic and Mythic, even when several thresholds are crossed together.

Alpha 1.0.37 (a wider circle of protection)

  • Protection that reaches: Battlefield Ministry now expands Guardian Embrace, Consecrated Ground, both Blessings and Heaven's Trumpet. Their accepted cast boundaries match trained reach while retaining target-body, allegiance and dungeon-wall rules.
  • A circle that stays with you: Guardian Embrace has a persistent healing perimeter that follows the caster without enlarging its body-sized decorations. Players joining mid-cast receive its trained radius and remaining time.
  • Holy ground, clearly marked: Consecrated Ground's healing and damage use its trained area, including the Expanded rune. Its persistent circle matches that area for the caster and observers.
  • More dependable offline support: Guardian healing uses the server's base amount and healing bonuses; holy ground remains visible until expiry. Support includes the caster and filters hostile actors. Heaven's Trumpet now deals its base damage and respects dungeon walls and stun immunity.
  • No doubled local healing: Multiplayer Guardian Embrace relies on server healing instead of also running the offline healing loop. These repairs do not complete the broader talent, offline-parity or phone-layout work.

Alpha 1.0.36 (the reach of your training)

  • Reach worth investing in: Range talents now affect Teleport, Scorch Beam, Arcane Missiles target acquisition, Weak Point Mark, Backstab and Shadow Lunge. Rune-adjusted reach and dungeon walls remain authoritative, and general talents remain visible after choosing a desktop specialization.
  • Boundaries you can trust: Flame Whip, Gravity Well, Meteor Drop and Inferno Cataclysm use their trained dimensions for gameplay and visible boundaries. Accepted casts correct stale predictions without replaying the animation; remote players see the resolved footprint without needing your private talent ranks. Delayed Meteor impacts retain their original trained size.
  • Wounds that keep working: Shadow Lunge applies its promised bleed, and bleeding and poison now tick on enemies with damage attribution and normal kill rewards. Spreading poison respects dungeon walls.
  • The enemy you chose: Desktop hotbar casts retain the hovered actor's identity, including when briefly buffered by a cooldown. Shadow Lunge no longer falls back to a different nearby enemy because the hotbar discarded its target.
  • A wider cleansing circle: Battlefield Ministry expands Purifying Wave from 8m to 9.2m at five ranks, with matching rings at both graphics settings. Offline cleansing includes yourself, clears poison and roots, and does not cleanse enemies or PvP opponents.
  • Cleaner offline spell behavior: Ground spells respect placement range and dungeon floor before spending resources. Gravity Well pulls and damages once, Inferno uses its ordinary one-second cadence, and falling Meteors impact the selected ground point with body-aware, wall-safe hit checks.
